### Common pitfalls
- **Continuity of the derivative matters.** $f(x)=x+2x^2\sin(1/x)$, $f(0)=0$, has $f'(0)=1$ but is injective on no interval containing $0$, because $f'$ is discontinuous at $0$. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_function_theorem))
- **The condition is sufficient, not necessary, for a continuous inverse.** $x\mapsto x^3$ is a bijection of $\mathbb R$ with $f'(0)=0$; its inverse $\sqrt[3]{y}$ exists but is not differentiable at $0$. ([Dontchev–Rockafellar, §1A and §1C](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~rtr/papers/rtr208-ImplicitFns-DontRock.pdf))
- **Local is not global.** A nonvanishing Jacobian determinant everywhere does not give injectivity (the exponential example); global conclusions need properness or growth hypotheses such as Hadamard's. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_function_theorem); [De Marco–Gorni–Zampieri](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1410.7902))
- **Real and complex cases differ.** An injective holomorphic map has a holomorphic inverse, but an injective smooth real map need not have a differentiable one. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_function_theorem))
- **Fréchet spaces.** In Nash–Moser, invertibility of the linearization at a single point is not enough; it is required on a whole neighbourhood, with tame estimates. ([Wikipedia, Nash–Moser theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash%E2%80%93Moser_theorem))
- **Weak ordered fields.** Over some Archimedean ordered fields other than $\mathbb R$ the theorem fails, and constructively the usual mean-value proof needs uniform differentiability. ([nLab](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/inverse+function+theorem))

### Open problems
- **Jacobian conjecture in dimension two.** The conjecture is the polynomial analogue of the theorem: a polynomial map $F:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^n$ whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero constant should have a polynomial inverse. It was stated for two variables by Kraus (1884) and extended to $n$ variables by Keller (1939). nLab reports an explicit counterexample for $n=3$ announced by Alpöge in July 2026: a map with Jacobian determinant $-2$ everywhere and $F(0,0,-\tfrac14)=F(1,-\tfrac32,\tfrac{13}2)=F(-1,\tfrac32,\tfrac{13}2)$; it implies counterexamples for all $n\ge3$, and the conjecture remains open for $n=2$ ([nLab, Jacobian conjecture](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Jacobian+conjecture)). This status change rests on an announcement and unrefereed preprints, not yet on journal publication: Meng and Yang (July 2026) cite Alpöge's refutation of the three-variable case and list $JC_2$ as unsettled ([Meng–Yang, arXiv:2607.22198](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22198)), and Gao constructs further, inequivalent counterexamples in dimensions above two and leaves open a complete classification of the fibres of four of his maps ([Gao, arXiv:2608.00222](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00222)).
- **Hessian conjecture in dimension four.** The same preprint claims a five-variable counterexample to the Hessian conjecture, which with earlier results would settle it in every dimension except $n=4$, and shows that $HC_4$ implies $JC_2$; this is likewise unrefereed. ([Meng–Yang, arXiv:2607.22198](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22198))
- **Set-valued Nash–Moser.** Dontchev and Rockafellar call extending the Nash–Moser theorem to set-valued mappings, in the setting of their metric-regularity inverse theorems, "a challenging avenue for future research". ([Dontchev–Rockafellar, §5 commentary](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~rtr/papers/rtr208-ImplicitFns-DontRock.pdf))

### Resources
- **Reference:** [Wikipedia, Inverse function theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_function_theorem): statements in $\mathbb R^n$, Banach spaces, and the holomorphic case, the constant rank theorem, and counterexamples.
- **Reference:** [nLab, inverse function theorem](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/inverse+function+theorem): contraction proof and constructive or ordered-field versions.
- **Learn:** [MIT OCW 18.101, Lecture 6](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-101-analysis-ii-fall-2005/d2c8fc5fe57cd59efc99caa048983d4c_lecture6.pdf): Guillemin's $C^r$ statement and proof lemmas.
- **Learn:** [MIT OCW 18.117, Lecture 7](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-117-topics-in-several-complex-variables-spring-2005/989bea2ba42545febc2830a2b5f59cf2_18117_lec07.pdf): holomorphic inverse and implicit function theorems.
- **Primary:** [Dontchev–Rockafellar, Implicit Functions and Solution Mappings](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~rtr/papers/rtr208-ImplicitFns-DontRock.pdf): an author-hosted monograph covering the classical, strict, Lyusternik–Graves, and metric-regularity theorems, with historical commentary.
- **Primary:** [De Marco–Gorni–Zampieri, Global Inversion of Functions](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.7902): a survey of the Hadamard–Caccioppoli and Hadamard–Lévy theorems.
- **Primary:** [Phien, Quantitative Lipschitz inverse theorems](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.4916): quantitative forms of Clarke's theorem.
- **Further reading:** [Krantz and Parks, The Implicit Function Theorem: History, Theory, and Applications (Springer, 2013)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/978-1-4614-5981-1): monograph on history and generalizations.
- **Further reading:** [Dontchev and Rockafellar, Implicit Functions and Solution Mappings (Springer, 2014 edition)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/978-1-4939-1037-3): Springer Series in Operations Research and Financial Engineering.
- **Further reading:** [Hamilton, The inverse function theorem of Nash and Moser (Bull. AMS, 1982)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1090/S0273-0979-1982-15004-2): the standard exposition of Nash–Moser.
- **Further reading:** [Clarke, On the inverse function theorem (Pacific J. Math., 1976)](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2140/pjm.1976.64.97): the Lipschitz inverse theorem.
references.Israel Junction Conditions:
## Reference
### Overview
The Darmois–Israel junction conditions say when two solutions of the [Einstein Field Equations](node:Einstein%20Field%20Equations) can be glued along a non-null hypersurface $\Sigma$. They also say what matter must live on $\Sigma$ when they are glued. The first condition is continuity of the induced metric. The second relates the jump in [extrinsic curvature](node:Extrinsic%20Curvature) to the surface stress-energy $S_{ab}$ of a thin shell, through the Lanczos equation. Further identities fix the shell's energy balance. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1))

A boundary surface, with no shell, needs both the first and second fundamental forms to be continuous: these are the Darmois conditions (1927). Lake notes that they agree with the Lichnerowicz conditions in Gaussian-normal coordinates but not under loose definitions of "admissible" coordinates, and that Israel gave the correct proof. ([Lake 2017](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1705.01090))

Shells modelled this way include domain walls, brane-worlds and impulsive waves ([Senovilla 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.03582)), false-vacuum bubble walls ([Aguirre & Johnson 2005](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0508093)) and cut-and-paste wormholes ([Garcia, Lobo & Visser 2012](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1112.2057)). In braneworlds the junction conditions follow from integrating the 5D field equations across the brane and fix the brane's extrinsic curvature in terms of brane matter. ([Maartens & Koyama, PDF §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.3962v2))

### Formal definition
Let $\Sigma$ be timelike with induced metric $\gamma_{ab}$, outward-pointing spacelike unit normal $n^\mu$ (from $\mathcal V^-$ to $\mathcal V^+$), and tangent basis $e^\mu_{(a)}$. Gonçalves defines $K_{ab}=-n_\mu e^\nu_{(b)}\nabla_\nu e^\mu_{(a)}$, the jump $[X]=X^+-X^-$, and the average $\{X\}=\tfrac12(X^++X^-)$. In units $G=c=1$ ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1)):

1. **First junction condition:** $[\gamma_{ab}]=0$. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1))
2. **Lanczos equation** ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1)):
$$[K_{ab}]-\gamma_{ab}[K]=-8\pi S_{ab},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad [K_{ab}]=-8\pi\left(S_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\gamma_{ab}\right).$$
3. **Conservation equation:** ${}^{3}\nabla_bS^b{}_a=-[e^\mu_{(a)}T_{\mu\nu}n^\nu]$. It follows by taking the divergence of the Lanczos equation $S^b{}_a=-\tfrac1{8\pi}([K^b{}_a]-\delta^b_a[K])$ and using the Codazzi (momentum) constraint $G_{\mu\nu}e^\mu_{(a)}n^\nu=K^b{}_{a|b}-K_{,a}$ on each side. ([Garcia, Lobo & Visser 2012](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1112.2057), eqs. (19), (26)) Gonçalves (eq. 14) and Garcia, Lobo and Visser (eq. 27) print this identity with a plus sign, which does not follow from the equations they combine. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1); [Garcia, Lobo & Visser 2012](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1112.2057))
4. **Normal–normal equation:** $S^{ab}\{K_{ab}\}=[T_{\mu\nu}n^\mu n^\nu]$. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1))

Equations 3 and 4 are identities that follow from the constraint equations; they are not independent dynamics. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1)) Garcia, Lobo and Visser use the same structure, with normals pointing from the $-$ to the $+$ manifold and $n_\mu n^\mu=+1$. ([Garcia, Lobo & Visser 2012](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1112.2057))

**Five dimensions.** For a brane in a 5D bulk with $\kappa_5^2$ the 5D coupling, the trace coefficient changes to $1/3$ ([Maartens & Koyama, PDF §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.3962v2)):
$$g^+_{\mu\nu}-g^-_{\mu\nu}=0,\qquad K^+_{\mu\nu}-K^-_{\mu\nu}=-\kappa_5^2\left[T^{\rm brane}_{\mu\nu}-\tfrac13T^{\rm brane}g_{\mu\nu}\right],\qquad T^{\rm brane}_{\mu\nu}=T_{\mu\nu}-\lambda g_{\mu\nu}.$$
In general dimension, for a non-null shell with $n\cdot n=\epsilon$ in canonical gauge, the singular Einstein part is $\mathcal G_{\beta\mu}=-[K_{\beta\mu}]+(g_{\beta\mu}-\epsilon n_\beta n_\mu)[K^\rho{}_\rho]$. ([Senovilla 2018](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1805.03582))

### Key results
- **Distributional origin.** If the metric is continuous with a kink, then in an adapted coordinate $y$ second derivatives split as $a''=\widehat{a''}+[a']\delta(y)$. Matching the $\delta$-part of the Einstein tensor to the $\delta$-localized brane source gives the junction conditions. ([Binétruy, Deffayet & Langlois 1999](https://arxiv.org/html/hep-th/9905012v2)) The derivation is the matching of singular parts of [distributions](node:Distributions%20%28Generalized%20Functions%29).
- **$Z_2$-symmetric brane.** Reflection symmetry gives $K^-_{\mu\nu}=-K^+_{\mu\nu}$, so $K_{\mu\nu}=-\tfrac12\kappa_5^2\left[T_{\mu\nu}+\tfrac13(\lambda-T)g_{\mu\nu}\right]$ on the brane. Substituting into the Gauss equation gives the [effective brane Einstein equations](node:Effective%20Einstein%20Equations%20on%20the%20Brane). ([Maartens & Koyama, PDF §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.3962v2))
- **Spherical dust shell.** For vacuum regions with Schwarzschild masses $m_-$ inside and $M=m_++m_-$ outside, a dust shell has $\dot\sigma/\sigma+2\dot R/R=0$, so its rest mass $m_\Sigma=4\pi R^2\sigma$ is constant. It obeys
$$\dot R^2=\left(\frac{m_+}{m_\Sigma}\right)^2-1+\frac{M+m_-}{R}+\frac{m_\Sigma^2}{4R^2}.$$
With tangential pressure the conservation law becomes $\dot\sigma+2(\dot R/R)(\sigma+p)=0$. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1)) For shells with a linear equation of state $p=\alpha\sigma$, $-1<\alpha<1$, there are no stable solutions. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0212124))
- **Null shells (Barrabès–Israel).** For a null hypersurface with generators $k^\alpha$, continuous metric and continuous induced metric $[\sigma_{AB}]=0$, the shell's stress-energy is $T^{\alpha\beta}_\Sigma=(-k_\mu u^\mu)^{-1}S^{\alpha\beta}\delta(\tau)$, with
$$S^{\alpha\beta}=\mu k^\alpha k^\beta+j^A\left(k^\alpha e^\beta_A+e^\alpha_Ak^\beta\right)+p\,\sigma^{AB}e^\alpha_Ae^\beta_B,$$
$$\mu=-\tfrac1{8\pi}\sigma^{AB}[C_{AB}],\qquad j^A=\tfrac1{8\pi}\sigma^{AB}[C_{\lambda B}],\qquad p=-\tfrac1{8\pi}[C_{\lambda\lambda}].$$
Here $C_{ab}$ is the transverse curvature, $[C_{ab}]=\tfrac12\gamma_{\alpha\beta}e^\alpha_ae^\beta_b$ with $\gamma_{\alpha\beta}=[g_{\alpha\beta,\gamma}]N^\gamma$, and $\lambda$ labels the null direction. This is Poisson's reformulation of Barrabès and Israel (1991). ([Poisson 2002](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0207101))
- **Thin-shell wormholes need negative energy.** In cut-and-paste constructions that glue two copies of a static spherically symmetric spacetime at a throat, the surface energy density $\sigma$ is always negative. Linear stability is then equivalent to choosing suitable properties for the exotic throat material. ([Garcia, Lobo & Visser 2012](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1112.2057))
- **Beyond GR.** In theories quadratic in curvature, shells generically carry a double-layer term with an external energy flux and an external scalar pressure or tension, all needed for a divergence-free total stress-energy. Matching without a shell is stricter than in GR. ([Reina, Senovilla & Vera 2016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.05515))

### Examples
- **Brane cosmology.** For $ds^2=-n^2d\tau^2+a^2\delta_{ij}dx^idx^j+b^2dy^2$ with brane density $\rho$ and pressure $p$, the junction conditions read $[a']/(a_0b_0)=-\kappa_5^2\rho/3$ and $[n']/(n_0b_0)=\kappa_5^2(3p+2\rho)/3$. In their exact brane solution the expansion obeys $\dot a_0^2/a_0^2=\kappa_5^4\rho^2/36$, quadratic in $\rho$. ([Binétruy, Deffayet & Langlois 1999](https://arxiv.org/html/hep-th/9905012v2)) The same matching underlies the [Randall–Sundrum](node:Randall–Sundrum%20Model) and [DGP](node:DGP%20Gravity) Friedmann equations. ([Maartens & Koyama, PDF §9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.3962v2))
- **False-vacuum bubbles.** For a thin wall of surface energy density $\sigma$ separating a [de Sitter](node:de%20Sitter%20Space) interior ($a_{ds}=1-\Lambda_-r^2/3$) from a Schwarzschild–de Sitter exterior ($a_{sds}=1-2M/r-\Lambda_+r^2/3$), the junction condition is $\beta_{ds}-\beta_{sds}=4\pi\sigma r$ with $\beta_{ds}=-a_{ds}\,dt/d\tau$ and $\beta_{sds}=a_{sds}\,dt/d\tau$. Under spherical symmetry the dynamics reduce to the wall radius. ([Aguirre & Johnson 2005](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0508093))
- **Matching to [Schwarzschild](node:Schwarzschild%20Solution) exteriors.** Gonçalves matches two arbitrary spherical spacetimes across a shell, and reduces the relative motion of two dust shells to that of one shell with different masses on each side. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0212124))

### History
Darmois gave the boundary-surface conditions in 1927, in "Les équations de la gravitation einsteinienne" (Mémorial des Sciences Mathématiques XXV). Lichnerowicz's version appears in his 1939 and 1955 works. ([Lake 2017](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1705.01090)) Senovilla describes Lanczos's work on shells as pioneering. ([Senovilla 2018](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1805.03582))

Israel submitted "Singular hypersurfaces and thin shells in general relativity" in fall 1965 ([Lake 2017](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1705.01090)). It appeared in Il Nuovo Cimento B 44 (1), pp. 1–14, July 1966 ([Crossref](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1007/BF02710419)) and is Israel's most cited paper ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_Israel)). The lightlike case was treated by Barrabès and Israel, "Thin shells in general relativity and cosmology: The lightlike limit", Phys. Rev. D 43, 1129–1142 (1991) ([Crossref](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1103/PhysRevD.43.1129)). Poisson calls it the definitive treatment. ([Poisson 2002](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0207101))

### Connections
- [Einstein Field Equations](node:Einstein%20Field%20Equations): their $\delta$-function part is the Lanczos equation.
- [Extrinsic Curvature](node:Extrinsic%20Curvature): its jump is fixed by $S_{ab}$.
- [Distributions (Generalized Functions)](node:Distributions%20%28Generalized%20Functions%29): thin shells are $\delta$-supported sources.
- [Gauss–Codazzi Equations](node:Gauss–Codazzi%20Equations): the energy and normal–normal equations are the Codazzi and Gauss constraints across $\Sigma$.
- [Effective Einstein Equations on the Brane](node:Effective%20Einstein%20Equations%20on%20the%20Brane) and [Braneworld Cosmology](node:Braneworld%20Cosmology): built from the $Z_2$ junction condition.
- [Randall–Sundrum Model](node:Randall–Sundrum%20Model) and [DGP Gravity](node:DGP%20Gravity): brane Friedmann equations.
- [Energy Conditions](node:Energy%20Conditions): thin-shell wormholes violate them at the throat.
- [de Sitter Space](node:de%20Sitter%20Space), [Schwarzschild Solution](node:Schwarzschild%20Solution) and [Black Holes](node:Black%20Holes): typical regions glued across shells.
- [General Relativity](node:General%20Relativity): the theory in which the standard conditions hold.

### Common pitfalls
- **Signs are convention-laden.** The sign of $K_{ab}$, the orientation of $n^\mu$, and the order of the jump all change signs. Israel's formalism requires the normal to point from $-$ to $+$. ([Garcia, Lobo & Visser 2012](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1112.2057); [Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1))
- **The trace coefficient depends on dimension.** It is $\tfrac12$ for a 3-dimensional shell in 4D and $\tfrac13$ for a 4-dimensional brane in 5D. ([Gonçalves 2002](https://arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0212124v1); [Maartens & Koyama, PDF §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.3962v2))
- **Null shells need a different formalism.** The induced metric of a null hypersurface is degenerate (effectively two-dimensional), so null shells are described with the transverse curvature $C_{ab}$ and the nondegenerate transverse metric $\sigma_{AB}$. ([Poisson 2002](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/0207101))
- **"Darmois" and "Lichnerowicz" are not interchangeable.** They are equivalent in Gaussian-normal coordinates. Under loose definitions of admissible coordinates the Lichnerowicz conditions add restrictions, some gauge and some physical. ([Lake 2017](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1705.01090))
- **Junction conditions do not close brane dynamics.** On a $Z_2$ brane they fix $K_{\mu\nu}$, but the projected bulk Weyl tensor still requires solving the bulk. ([Maartens & Koyama, PDF §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.3962v2))

### Open problems
- **Consequences of the full shell equations.** Senovilla derives the complete set of field equations for shells of arbitrary causal character and dimension. The full set had not been considered before, and he states that results on shells, branes, domain walls and impulsive waves "may have to be revisited and/or completed". For non-null shells, the restrictions the new algebraic relations impose "remain to be analyzed in full generality". The new null-shell equations "remain to be studied in depth". ([Senovilla 2018](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1805.03582))

### Resources
- **Reference:** [Werner Israel (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werner_Israel): context for the 1966 and 1991 shell papers.
- **Learn:** [Maartens & Koyama, Brane-World Gravity, §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1004.3962v2): derivation of the 5D junction conditions and their use on a $Z_2$ brane.
- **Primary:** [Gonçalves, Relativistic shells: Dynamics, horizons, and shell crossing](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0212124): full non-null formalism and spherical shells.
- **Primary:** [Poisson, A reformulation of the Barrabès–Israel null-shell formalism](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0207101): null shells.
- **Primary:** [Senovilla, Equations for general shells](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.03582): complete equations for shells of any causal type.
- **Primary:** [Garcia, Lobo & Visser, thin-shell traversable wormholes (2012)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2057): cut-and-paste wormholes and stability.
- **Further reading:** [Poisson, A Relativist's Toolkit (Cambridge, 2004), ch. 3 "Hypersurfaces"](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/relativists-toolkit/notation-and-conventions/A35B04ED0EC0C68DBB44F2EDF11E9D81): the standard graduate treatment of hypersurfaces.
references.Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures:
## Reference
### Overview
A joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) is a self-supervised learning design in which two inputs $x$ and $y$ are each mapped to a representation, $s_x$ and $s_y$, and a predictor, possibly conditioned on a latent or auxiliary variable $z$, predicts $s_y$ from $s_x$; the training loss is measured in representation space, not in pixel or token space. Yann LeCun introduced JEPAs in 2022 as part of a proposal for autonomous machine intelligence, and they differ from autoencoders in operating entirely in latent space, predicting masked latent representations from visible context. ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-supervised_learning); [Dawid and LeCun 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.02572))

The design sits between two older families. Joint-embedding architectures (Siamese-style invariance methods such as Barlow Twins, VICReg, BYOL) learn similar embeddings for augmented views of the same input; generative architectures such as masked autoencoders reconstruct the missing part of the signal $y$ in input space. A JEPA keeps the predictor and the conditioning variable of the generative approach but applies the loss in embedding space, so it does not seek invariance to hand-crafted augmentations and does not have to model every unpredictable detail of $y$. ([Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08243); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-supervised_learning))

The main instantiations are I-JEPA for images, V-JEPA for video, and V-JEPA 2, which adds an action-conditioned predictor used as a latent world model for robot planning. The motivation from the energy-based viewpoint is that pixel-level prediction of continuous signals is multimodal (there are many ways to fill in a masked region), while prediction in a learned representation lets the encoders discard irrelevant detail. ([Dawid and LeCun 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.02572); [Assran et al. 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09985))

### Formal definition
**Energy-based form.** A JEPA is an energy-based model with encoders $s_x = \mathrm{Enc}_{w_1}(x)$, $s_y = \mathrm{Enc}_{w_2}(y)$ (which may differ in architecture and need not share parameters), a predictor $\mathrm{Pred}_{w_3}$, and a latent $z$; its energy is
$$F_w(x,y,z) = D\big(s_y,\ \mathrm{Pred}_{w_3}(s_x, z)\big),$$
a distance between the predicted and actual representation of $y$. Training minimizes the prediction error together with regularizers that maximize the information content of $s_x$ about $x$ and of $s_y$ about $y$ (to prevent collapse) and minimize the information content $R(z)$ of the latent. ([Dawid and LeCun 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.02572))

**I-JEPA (masked image form).** An image $y$ is split into $N$ patches and passed through a target encoder $f_{\bar\theta}$ to give $s_y=\{s_{y_1},\dots,s_{y_N}\}$. $M$ target blocks with masks $B_1,\dots,B_M$ are sampled from the *output* of the target encoder; a context block $x$ with mask $B_x$ (overlaps with targets removed) is encoded by the context encoder $f_\theta$. For each block, a predictor $g_\phi$ receives $s_x$ and mask tokens $\{m_j\}_{j\in B_i}$ (a shared learnable vector plus positional embedding) and outputs $\hat s_y(i)$. The loss is
$$\mathcal L = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{i=1}^{M}\sum_{j\in B_i}\big\|\hat s_{y_j} - s_{y_j}\big\|_2^2 ,$$
with $\theta,\phi$ trained by [gradient descent](node:Gradient%20Descent) and $\bar\theta$ an exponential moving average of $\theta$. ([Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08243))

### Key results
- **Representation collapse and its remedies.** For any joint-embedding design the trivial solution in which the encoder outputs a constant (a flat energy landscape) minimizes the prediction loss; JEPAs share this problem with invariance methods. It is avoided either by regularizers that maximize information content (VICReg: hinge on per-dimension standard deviation, penalty on off-diagonal covariance) or by an asymmetric architecture between the $x$- and $y$-encoders (I-JEPA uses an exponential-moving-average target encoder). ([Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08243); [Dawid and LeCun 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.02572))
- **Implicit bias toward high-influence features (Littwin et al. 2024).** For centered $x,y$ with diagonal $\Sigma^{xx},\Sigma^{yx}$, feature covariance $\lambda_i=\Sigma^{yx}_{ii}$ and regression coefficient $\rho_i=\lambda_i/\Sigma^{xx}_{ii}$, a depth-$L$ linear encoder trained by gradient flow from a small initialization (each layer $\varepsilon^{1/L}$ times an orthogonal matrix, $0<\varepsilon\ll 1$) satisfies $\dot w = w^{3-1/L}\lambda - w^3\lambda/\rho$ under the JEPA loss $\tfrac12\mathbb E\|V\bar W x - \mathrm{SG}(\bar W)y\|^2$ and $\dot w = w^{2-1/L}\lambda - w^3\lambda/\rho$ under the MAE loss. MAE learns features greedily in order of $\lambda$; for $L>1$ JEPA additionally prioritizes large $\rho$, more strongly with depth, and can reverse the MAE order. ([Littwin et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.03475))
- **Masking design matters (I-JEPA).** Semantic representations required large target blocks (four blocks, scale $0.15$–$0.2$, aspect ratio $0.75$–$1.5$) and an informative context block (scale $0.85$–$1.0$); in the paper's ablation, low-shot ImageNet accuracy dropped from 54.2% to 9.0% when only one target block was used. ([Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08243))
- **Efficiency and accuracy without augmentations.** A ViT-H/14 I-JEPA trained on ImageNet used under 1,200 GPU hours, over 2.5 times faster than a ViT-S/16 trained with iBOT, and reached 79.3% linear-probe accuracy (81.1% for ViT-H/16 at $448^2$), above MAE's 77.2% for a ViT-H/14 trained 1,600 epochs. ([Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08243))
- **Isotropic Gaussian embeddings (LeJEPA).** Balestriero and LeCun argue that the isotropic Gaussian is the embedding distribution minimizing downstream prediction risk, and enforce it with Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization (SIGReg), removing stop-gradient and teacher-student heuristics; a ViT-H/14 reached 79% ImageNet linear accuracy. ([Balestriero and LeCun 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08544))

### Examples
- **V-JEPA.** Feature prediction alone (no pretrained image encoder, text, negatives, or reconstruction), trained on 2 million videos; a frozen ViT-H/16 reached 81.9% on Kinetics-400, 72.2% on Something-Something-v2, and 77.9% on ImageNet-1K. ([Bardes et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08471))
- **V-JEPA 2 and V-JEPA 2-AC.** Pretrained on over one million hours of video and images (77.3 top-1 on SSv2), then post-trained as an action-conditioned predictor on under 62 hours of DROID robot video. Planning encodes current and goal images, scores candidate action sequences by the L1 distance between predicted and goal representations, optimizes them with the cross-entropy method, and executes the first action in receding-horizon fashion; it achieved zero-shot pick-and-place on Franka arms in two labs. ([Assran et al. 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09985); [V-JEPA 2 HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.09985))
- **H-JEPA.** Stacking JEPAs so that a low level makes short-horizon detailed predictions and a higher level makes longer-horizon predictions from coarser representations, intended for multiscale planning. ([Dawid and LeCun 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.02572))

### History
LeCun proposed JEPAs in 2022 within an architecture for autonomous intelligence; his Les Houches 2022 lectures, written up by Dawid and LeCun in June 2023, present JEPA and its hierarchical form H-JEPA as the core building block. I-JEPA (Assran et al., posted January 2023, published at CVPR 2023) was the first large-scale image instance, followed by V-JEPA (February 2024), V-JEPA 2 (June 2025), and LeJEPA (November 2025). ([Dawid and LeCun 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02572); [Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08243); [Crossref, CVPR 2023](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/CVPR52729.2023.01499); [Bardes et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08471); [Balestriero and LeCun 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08544))

### Connections
- [Self-Supervised and Contrastive Learning](node:Self-Supervised%20and%20Contrastive%20Learning): JEPA is a non-generative, predictive member of the self-supervised family.
- [Masked Autoencoders](node:Masked%20Autoencoders): the generative counterpart, predicting pixels instead of embeddings; the Littwin et al. analysis compares the two directly.
- [Energy-Based Models](node:Energy-Based%20Models): the framework in which JEPA is defined, with energy given by representation-space prediction error.
- [Contrastive Collapse and Negative Sampling](node:Contrastive%20Collapse%20and%20Negative%20Sampling): collapse is the central failure mode JEPA training has to prevent.
- [World Models](node:World%20Models): action-conditioned JEPAs (V-JEPA 2-AC) serve as latent world models.
- [Latent Predictive Planning](node:Latent%20Predictive%20Planning): planning by optimizing actions against a latent goal energy.
- [Model Predictive Control](node:Model%20Predictive%20Control): V-JEPA 2-AC uses receding-horizon planning with the cross-entropy method.
- [Vision Transformers](node:Vision%20Transformers): the encoder and predictor backbone in I-JEPA and V-JEPA.
- [Deep Learning](node:Deep%20Learning): the underlying training methodology.

### Common pitfalls
- **Masking the input versus the output.** In I-JEPA the target blocks are masked on the output of the target encoder, not the input; the authors call this distinction crucial for high-level targets. ([Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08243))
- **Assuming the predictor prevents collapse by itself.** The prediction loss alone admits constant encoders; an EMA target, stop-gradient, or an explicit information regularizer is required. ([Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08243); [Balestriero and LeCun 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08544))
- **Confusing JEPA with joint-embedding invariance methods.** JEAs learn invariance to augmentations; JEPAs learn representations predictive of each other given $z$. ([Assran et al. 2023](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.08243))

### Open problems
- **Long-horizon planning with JEPA world models.** The V-JEPA 2 authors state that long-horizon planning is limited by error accumulation in autoregressive rollouts and exponential growth of the search space, and that it is needed for tasks such as pick-and-place without image sub-goals; they also list language goal specification and camera-pose sensitivity as open issues. ([V-JEPA 2 HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.09985))
- **Theory beyond linear models.** Littwin et al. state that extending their implicit-bias results to nonlinear models and realistic data distributions is unexplored. ([Littwin et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.03475))

### Resources
- **Reference:** [Self-supervised learning (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-supervised_learning): describes JEPA alongside contrastive, non-contrastive, and joint-embedding methods.
- **Learn:** [Dawid and LeCun, Introduction to Latent Variable Energy-Based Models (Les Houches lecture notes)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02572): energy-based models, regularized training, JEPA and H-JEPA.
- **Primary:** [Assran et al. 2023, I-JEPA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08243): the first large-scale JEPA for images.
- **Primary:** [Littwin et al. 2024, How JEPA Avoids Noisy Features](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.03475): gradient-flow analysis of JEPA versus MAE.
- **Further reading:** [Balestriero et al. 2023, A Cookbook of Self-Supervised Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.12210): foundations and recent SSL methods, with the role of each design choice explained.
references.Kaluza–Klein Dark Matter:
## Reference
### Overview
Kaluza–Klein (KK) dark matter is the proposal that the dark matter is the lightest Kaluza–Klein particle (LKP), a heavy partner of a Standard Model particle that carries momentum in a compact extra dimension. The idea arises in models with **universal extra dimensions** (UED), in which all fields propagate in the extra dimensions; in the ADD model, by contrast, Standard Model fields are confined to a four-dimensional brane and only gravity propagates in the bulk. ([Wikipedia: Universal extra dimensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_extra_dimension))

In UED, momentum conservation in the extra dimension becomes KK-number conservation. The orbifold needed for chiral fermions breaks it, but a remnant $Z_2$, **KK parity**, can survive and make the LKP stable, much as R-parity stabilizes the lightest superpartner. ([Hooper, TASI 2008 lectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4090)) Cheng, Feng and Matchev described stable KK partners in UED as "the only specific dark matter candidate to emerge from theories with extra dimensions" at the time. ([Cheng, Feng & Matchev](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0207125))

The LKP is a weakly interacting massive particle whose thermal relic abundance comes out right for masses near the TeV scale, which makes it a competitor to supersymmetric neutralinos testable at colliders and in direct and indirect detection. ([Hooper & Profumo](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0701197)) Recasts of 13 TeV LHC searches showed the minimal model "getting in tension with observation" ([Deutschmann, Flacke & Kim](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00410)), and the PDG reports it ruled out once LHC data are combined with the relic density, while extensions with boundary terms can remain compatible. ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf))

### Formal definition
In minimal UED (MUED) one extra dimension of radius $R\sim\mathrm{TeV}^{-1}$ is compactified on the orbifold $S^1/Z_2$, and each Standard Model field $X$ becomes a tower of KK states with tree-level masses
$$m^2_{X^{(n)}}=\frac{n^2}{R^2}+m^2_{X^{(0)}},$$
where $X^{(0)}$ is the ordinary zero-mode particle. ([Hooper, TASI lectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4090)) The spectrum depends on $R$ and on the cutoff $\Lambda$ of the 5D theory, because quantum corrections sensitive to $\Lambda R$ split the KK masses. ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf))

**KK parity** is the $Z_2$ under which only odd-$n$ KK modes are charged, $P=(-1)^n$. It is conserved in UED if no explicit KK-parity-violating interactions are introduced on the orbifold fixed points. Then odd states are produced in pairs and the lightest odd state, the LKP, is stable. ([Hooper & Profumo](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0701197)) In the PDG description KK parity interchanges the two boundaries of the orbifold. ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf))

**KK dark matter** is the LKP produced as a thermal relic. It must be electrically neutral and colorless; candidates are the first KK excitations of the photon, $Z$, neutrinos, Higgs, or graviton. ([Hooper, TASI lectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4090))

### Key results
- **Loose electroweak bounds.** Because KK number is conserved, KK states contribute to electroweak observables only through loops, so the compactification scale could be as low as 300 GeV for one universal extra dimension; for two, the bound depends logarithmically on the cutoff. ([Appelquist, Cheng & Dobrescu](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0012100))
- **One-loop mass splittings make $B^{(1)}$ the LKP.** At tree level all level-$n$ masses are $n/R$ up to zero-mode masses, so decays sit at threshold and radiative corrections decide the spectrum. Cheng, Matchev and Schmaltz computed the complete one-loop corrections. On $S^1/Z_2$ the bulk corrections are $\delta m^2_{B_n}=-\tfrac{39}{2}\tfrac{g'^2\zeta(3)}{16\pi^4R^2}$, $\delta m^2_{W_n}=-\tfrac52\tfrac{g_2^2\zeta(3)}{16\pi^4R^2}$, $\delta m^2_{g_n}=-\tfrac32\tfrac{g_3^2\zeta(3)}{16\pi^4R^2}$ and zero for fermions and the Higgs. Boundary terms, assumed to vanish at $\Lambda$, then add logarithmic corrections, e.g. $\bar\delta m^2_{B_n}=-\tfrac16 m_n^2\tfrac{g'^2}{16\pi^2}\ln\tfrac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}$ against $+\tfrac{23}{2}m_n^2\tfrac{g_3^2}{16\pi^2}\ln\tfrac{\Lambda^2}{\mu^2}$ for KK gluons. With $R^{-1}=500$ GeV and $\Lambda R=20$ the KK "photon" gets the smallest correction and is the lightest state at each level, and the other level-1 states promptly cascade to it. ([Cheng, Matchev & Schmaltz](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0204342))
- **The KK photon is almost pure $B^{(1)}$.** The level-1 $B$–$W^3$ mass matrix has off-diagonal entries $\tfrac14 g_1g_2v^2$; when the difference between the radiative shifts $\delta m^2_{B^{(1)}}$ and $\delta m^2_{W^{(1)}}$ exceeds these, the mixing is driven to $\sin^2\theta_{W,1}\sim10^{-3}$. ([Hooper, TASI lectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4090))
- **Annihilation.** $B^{(1)}$ annihilates mainly to fermion pairs by $t$-channel KK-fermion exchange, with
$$\sigma v(B^{(1)}B^{(1)}\to f\bar f)=\frac{95}{32{,}256}\sum_f\frac{N_c\,(Y^4_{f_L}+Y^4_{f_R})\,g_1^4}{\pi m^2_{B^{(1)}}}.$$
The rate scales with hypercharge to the fourth power, so most annihilations go to charged leptons. ([Hooper, TASI lectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4090))
- **Relic density.** For $B^{(1)}$ alone in five dimensions, Servant and Tait found $m_{KK}\sim900$–$1200$ GeV for $\Omega=0.33\pm0.035$, with overclosure above about 1.9 TeV. ([Servant & Tait](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0206071)) Including level-2 states, which decay dominantly into Standard Model particles and feed [coannihilation](node:Coannihilation) of level-1 KK leptons, raises the preferred scale to $R^{-1}=1.3$ TeV, with LKP–nucleon cross sections typically below $10^{-10}$ pb unless KK quarks are nearly degenerate with the LKP. ([Bélanger, Kakizaki & Pukhov](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.2577)) With coannihilation and second-level resonances, MUED gives the observed abundance for $1.25\ \mathrm{TeV}\lesssim R^{-1}\lesssim1.5\ \mathrm{TeV}$. ([Deutschmann, Flacke & Kim](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00410))
- **Unsuppressed indirect signals.** Majorana neutralino annihilation is chirality-suppressed, giving soft secondary positrons, photons and neutrinos; $B^{(1)}$ bosons annihilate to hard positrons, neutrinos and photons at unsuppressed rates. ([Cheng, Feng & Matchev](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0207125))
- **Collider status of MUED.** Recasts of ATLAS and CMS 13 TeV SUSY searches exclude $R^{-1}\approx1400$ GeV for $\Lambda R\sim10$, rising to about 1500 GeV with a K-factor of 1.5, so MUED is "getting in tension with observation". ([Deutschmann, Flacke & Kim](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00410)) The PDG review gives $1/R>1.4$–$1.5$ TeV for $\Lambda R$ in $5$–$35$ and reports that MUED is ruled out when LHC data are combined with the relic density. ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf))

### Examples
- **Direct detection today.** LZ's 4.2 tonne-year exposure sets world-leading spin-independent and spin-dependent WIMP–nucleon limits for masses $\ge9$ GeV, with the strongest spin-independent exclusion $2.2\times10^{-48}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ (90% CL) at 40 GeV. ([LZ Collaboration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17036)) MUED LKP–nucleon cross sections, for TeV-scale LKPs, are typically below $10^{-10}$ pb ($10^{-46}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$). ([Bélanger, Kakizaki & Pukhov](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.2577))
- **KK photon versus KK neutrino.** Servant and Tait computed relic densities for both $B^{(1)}$ and $\nu^{(1)}$ LKPs. ([Servant & Tait](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0206071)) KK neutrinos are excluded by direct detection, as are sneutrinos and heavy fourth-generation Dirac neutrinos. ([Hooper, TASI lectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4090))
- **Six dimensions.** On $T^2/Z_2$ the dark-matter mass window shifts to about 650–850 GeV. ([Servant & Tait](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0206071))
- **Neutrinos from the Sun.** $B^{(1)}$ scatters on protons mainly spin-dependently, $\sigma_{B^{(1)}p,\rm SD}\approx1.8\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{pb}\,(m_{B^{(1)}}/\mathrm{TeV})^{-4}(\Delta/0.1)^{-2}$, where $\Delta$ is the fractional mass splitting to the KK quarks; this sets its solar capture rate. ([Hooper & Profumo](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0701197))
- **Non-minimal UED.** Boundary-localized terms on massive five-dimensional fields give zero and nonzero KK modes non-trivial extra-dimensional profiles, and nonzero terms strongly change the spectrum and couplings of the KK modes; in some parameter regions the LKP becomes the KK Higgs or the first KK $W^3$. ([Flacke, Menon & Phalen](https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.1598))
- **KK graviton superWIMP.** The level-1 graviton (or a right-handed KK neutrino) could also be the LKP; then the decay of the KK photon to it takes cosmological times. ([Cheng, Matchev & Schmaltz](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0204342)) Feng, Rajaraman and Takayama proposed such "superWIMPs", including KK-graviton dark matter in UED, which inherit the correct relic density from WIMP decay, escape conventional dark-matter searches, and can satisfy BBN and CMB bounds. ([Feng, Rajaraman & Takayama](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0302215))
- **Warped alternative.** In non-supersymmetric grand unified theories in warped extra dimensions, suppressing baryon-number violation can leave a stable KK particle with the gauge quantum numbers of a right-handed neutrino, stabilized by a combination of baryon number and color, with viable relic density from about 10 GeV to a few TeV. ([Agashe & Servant](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0403143))

### History
In 1919 Theodor Kaluza extended [general relativity](node:General%20Relativity) to five dimensions to unify gravity and electromagnetism. ([Hooper & Profumo](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0701197)) Appelquist, Cheng and Dobrescu (2001) proposed universal extra dimensions and showed that KK-number conservation weakens electroweak constraints. ([Appelquist, Cheng & Dobrescu](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0012100)) Cheng, Matchev and Schmaltz (2002) computed the radiative mass splittings that select $B^{(1)}$. ([Cheng, Matchev & Schmaltz](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0204342))

Servant and Tait computed the LKP relic density and proposed it as a viable dark-matter candidate. ([Servant & Tait](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0206071)) Cheng, Feng and Matchev then studied its direct and indirect detection. ([Cheng, Feng & Matchev](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0207125)) A 2014 status report found the roughly 1.4 TeV MUED dark-matter region untouched by LHC8 and beyond direct-detection reach, and expected LHC14 to probe it in the three-lepton channel. ([Servant, status report](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.4176)) Run 2 recasts in 2017 began to exclude that region. ([Deutschmann, Flacke & Kim](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00410))

### Connections
- [Universal Extra Dimensions](node:Universal%20Extra%20Dimensions): the framework in which the LKP and KK parity arise.
- [Extra Dimensions](node:Extra%20Dimensions): KK dark matter is the main dark-matter candidate from flat extra-dimension models.
- [Kaluza–Klein Modes](node:Kaluza–Klein%20Modes): the LKP is the lightest mode of a KK tower with masses near $n/R$.
- [Kaluza–Klein Theory](node:Kaluza–Klein%20Theory): the original five-dimensional idea behind KK towers.
- [Large Extra Dimensions](node:Large%20Extra%20Dimensions): in ADD only gravity propagates in the bulk, so there is no KK partner of SM matter.
- [Randall–Sundrum Model](node:Randall–Sundrum%20Model): warped models give different stable KK candidates.
- [Hierarchy Problem](node:Hierarchy%20Problem): UED, unlike warped models, does not address it.
- [Dark Matter](node:Dark%20Matter): KK dark matter is one proposed identity for it.
- [Weakly Interacting Massive Particles](node:Weakly%20Interacting%20Massive%20Particles): $B^{(1)}$ is a WIMP.
- [Thermal Freeze-Out](node:Thermal%20Freeze-Out): sets the LKP relic abundance.
- [Supersymmetry](node:Supersymmetry): KK parity plays the role of R-parity, and UED collider signals mimic SUSY.
- [Dark Matter Direct Detection](node:Dark%20Matter%20Direct%20Detection): LKP–nucleon scattering through KK-quark and Higgs exchange.
- [Dark Matter Indirect Detection](node:Dark%20Matter%20Indirect%20Detection): hard positrons, photons and solar neutrinos.
- [Collider Physics](node:Collider%20Physics): pair-produced KK states cascade to the LKP and give missing energy.
- [Orbifolds](node:Orbifolds): $S^1/Z_2$ allows chiral fermions and reduces KK number to KK parity.
- [Compactification](node:Compactification): the radius $R$ sets the LKP mass.
- [Grand Unification](node:Grand%20Unification): the warped-GUT stable KK particle.

### Common pitfalls
- **KK parity is an assumption.** Whether it holds depends on the compactification and UV completion; Servant and Tait note that it is preserved if the boundary Lagrangians at the two fixed points are symmetric. ([Servant & Tait](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0206071)) Without a UV completion one cannot say with certainty that it is conserved. ([Hooper & Profumo](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0701197))
- **The spectrum depends on boundary terms.** The finite parts of boundary counterterms are free parameters; the standard MUED spectrum assumes they vanish at $\Lambda$. ([Cheng, Matchev & Schmaltz](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0204342)) Nearly degenerate KK quarks and gluons raise the preferred $m_{B^{(1)}}$ while degenerate KK leptons lower it, so the optimal mass ranges from several hundred GeV to a few TeV. ([Cheng, Feng & Matchev](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0207125))
- **UED does not solve the [hierarchy problem](node:Hierarchy%20Problem).** ([Servant, status report](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.4176))
- **Collider signals look like SUSY.** KK states cascade to jets or leptons plus the invisible LKP, similar to R-parity-conserving SUSY signatures with [missing transverse momentum](node:Missing%20Transverse%20Momentum). ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf))

> [!warning] Contested
> **Cosmic-ray positron excesses.** $B^{(1)}$ annihilation was predicted to give hard positrons at unsuppressed rates. ([Cheng, Feng & Matchev](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0207125)) PAMELA and ATIC indicated a powerful source of energetic positrons and electrons within about 1 kpc, but its nature was unclear: pulsars are an alternative, and a dark-matter explanation needs annihilation rates hundreds or thousands of times above the naive thermal-relic value. ([Hooper, TASI lectures](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4090))

### Open problems
- **UV completion and KK parity.** Whether KK parity is conserved cannot be settled without a specific compactification scheme and a full UV completion of the theory; reviews proceed by assuming it. ([Hooper & Profumo](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0701197)) In extensions with boundary terms and bulk fermion masses, KK parity holds only if the boundary terms are chosen symmetric on both boundaries and the bulk masses KK-parity odd. ([Deutschmann, Flacke & Kim](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.00410))

### Resources
- **Reference:** [Universal extra dimensions (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_extra_dimension): overview of UED, $M_{KK}\approx R^{-1}$, and bounds.
- **Learn:** [D. Hooper, TASI 2008 Lectures on Dark Matter](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.4090): freeze-out, detection, and a section on KK dark matter.
- **Primary:** [G. Servant & T. Tait, "Is the Lightest Kaluza–Klein Particle a Viable Dark Matter Candidate?"](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0206071): the original relic-density calculation.
- **Primary:** [H.-C. Cheng, K. Matchev & M. Schmaltz, "Radiative Corrections to Kaluza-Klein Masses"](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0204342): the one-loop UED spectrum.
- **Primary:** [D. Hooper & S. Profumo, "Dark Matter and Collider Phenomenology of Universal Extra Dimensions"](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0701197): Physics Reports review of UED dark matter.
- **Further reading:** [PDG Review, "Extra Dimensions" (2024)](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf): current collider limits on UED and other extra-dimension models.
references.Kaluza–Klein Modes:
## Reference
### Overview
A field theory with compact [extra dimensions](node:Extra%20Dimensions) can be rewritten as a four-dimensional theory with infinitely many fields by a Kaluza–Klein (KK) reduction. A higher-dimensional field appears in 4D as a massless **zero mode** plus an infinite **tower** of massive copies, the KK modes; at energies below the compactification scale $1/R$ the massive modes can be neglected ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).

The modes are the Fourier components of the field along the compact space. Every excited mode has the same spin and quantum numbers as the parent field; they differ only in the KK number $n$, which labels the discrete fifth component of momentum, and the massive levels are degenerate while the zero mode is not ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)). On a general internal manifold the role of Fourier modes is played by eigenfunctions of the Laplacian ([Pope lecture notes](https://people.tamu.edu/~c-pope/ihplec.pdf)).

In the traditional picture the radius is near the Planck length, $10^{-33}$ cm, so the non-zero modes have masses of order the Planck mass, $10^{-5}$ g ([Pope lecture notes](https://people.tamu.edu/~c-pope/ihplec.pdf)). The ADD (1998) and Randall–Sundrum (1999) models instead put extra-dimension sizes between roughly a millimetre and $\sim$1/TeV, making KK states targets for colliders, astrophysics and short-range gravity tests ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).

### Formal definition
**Circle.** Take a complex scalar in flat 5D with $y\sim y+2\pi R$ ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)):
$$
S_5=-\int d^4x\,dy\,M_5\left[|\partial_\mu\phi|^2+|\partial_y\phi|^2+\lambda_5|\phi|^4\right],\qquad \phi(x,y)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi RM_5}}\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}e^{iny/R}\,\phi^{(n)}(x).
$$
Integrating over $y$ gives ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf))
$$
S_4=-\int d^4x\left[|\partial_\mu\phi^{(0)}|^2+\lambda_4|\phi^{(0)}|^4\right]-\int d^4x\sum_{n\neq0}\left[|\partial_\mu\phi^{(n)}|^2+\Big(\frac nR\Big)^2|\phi^{(n)}|^2\right]+\dots,\qquad \lambda_4=\frac{\lambda_5}{2\pi RM_5},
$$
so mode $n$ has mass $|n|/R$. A 5D bulk mass $m$ gives $m_n^2=m^2+n^2/R^2$ ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)).

**Torus.** On $T^\delta$ with equal radii the graviton expands as $G_{\mu\nu}(x,\vec y)=G^{(0)}_{\mu\nu}(x)+V_\delta^{-1/2}\sum_{\vec n\ne0}e^{i\vec n\cdot\vec y/R}G^{(\vec n)}_{\mu\nu}(x)$ with $m_{\vec n}^2=|\vec n|^2/R^2$, $\vec n\in\mathbb Z^\delta$ ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)). Levels are more degenerate than on a circle, and the number of KK states below a scale $\mu$ is approximately the volume of a $\delta$-ball of radius $\mu/M_c$ (with $M_c=1/R$) ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)):
$$
N(\mu,M_c)\simeq X_\delta\Big(\frac{\mu}{M_c}\Big)^{\delta},\qquad X_\delta=\frac{\pi^{\delta/2}}{\Gamma(1+\delta/2)}.
$$

**General compact spaces.** On an internal manifold $M$ the 4D-metric components are expanded in eigenfunctions $P^{(i)}(y)$ of the scalar Laplacian, starting with the constant zero-eigenvalue function, and the mixed components in vector eigenfunctions whose zero modes are the Killing vectors of $M$ ([Pope lecture notes](https://people.tamu.edu/~c-pope/ihplec.pdf)). On the sphere $S^{n-1}$, degree-$\ell$ harmonics satisfy $\Delta f=-\ell(\ell+n-2)f$ ([Wikipedia: Spherical harmonics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_harmonics)).

**Orbifolds.** On $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$ ($y\to-y$) each field is even or odd; even fields expand in $\cos(ny/R)$ and odd fields in $\sin(ny/R)$, so odd fields have no zero mode ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)).

**Scherk–Schwarz twist.** Requiring only $\phi(y+2\pi R)=e^{2\pi i\beta}\phi(y)$, with $\beta$ the Scherk–Schwarz charge, gives $\phi=e^{i\beta y/R}\sum_n\phi_n(x)e^{iny/R}$ and shifts the whole tower to $m_n=(n+\beta)/R$: every mode, including the would-be zero mode, is massive. Twisting by a symmetry can break global or gauge symmetries, and the mechanism can also break supersymmetry ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177); [PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).

### Key results
- **Volume-suppressed couplings.** The zero-mode coupling $\lambda_4=\lambda_5/(2\pi RM_5)$ decreases as $R$ grows, so for $R\gg1/M_5$ the massless scalar is very weakly coupled ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)). For gravity on $T^\delta$, $M_P^2=V_\delta M_D^{2+\delta}$, and each KK graviton couples with strength $1/M_P$ ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).
- **Energy regimes.** For $E\ll1/R$ physics is four-dimensional; for $1/R<E<M_*$ about $(ER)^\delta$ KK excitations are accessible; above $M_*$ the effective theory must be replaced by [quantum gravity](node:Quantum%20Gravity) ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)).
- **Gravity reduction.** In $4+n$ dimensions $h_{MN}$ splits into the 4D graviton $h_{\mu\nu}$, graviphotons $h_{a\mu}$ and graviscalars $h_{ab}$, whose trace is the radion ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)). For one circle, keeping $n=0$ gives $\frac{1}{2\kappa^2}\int d^4x\sqrt{-g}\,[R-\tfrac12(\partial\phi)^2-\tfrac14e^{-\sqrt3\phi}F^2]$, and the $n\ne0$ modes are massive spin-2 states with $m_n=|n|m$ and charge $e_n=n\sqrt2\kappa m$ ($m$ the inverse radius) ([Duff](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/hep-th/9410046)).
- **Massive KK vectors.** For a 5D abelian gauge field each $A^{(n)}_\mu$ gets mass $n/R$ by absorbing $A_5^{(n)}$, resembling the [Higgs Mechanism](node:Higgs%20Mechanism); a massless gauge field and a massless scalar $A_5^{(0)}$ remain ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)).
- **Fermions and the orbifold.** In odd dimensions there is no chirality. For a massless 5D fermion on $S^1$ the KK terms $(n/R)[\bar\psi_{n,L}\hat\psi_{n,R}-(L\leftrightarrow R)]$ pair even and odd modes and both zero modes stay massless; on $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$ one chirality is odd and projected out ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)). Because $\bar\Psi\Psi$ is odd under $y\to-y$, a *constant* 5D Dirac mass is forbidden, but an odd kink mass is allowed: $m_\Psi=c\,\sigma'=c\,k\,\epsilon(y)$, sourced by a scalar with odd kink VEV ([Gherghetta & Pomarol](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/hep-ph/0003129)).
- **Bulk-mass localization.** In a warped dimension, fermion zero modes vary as $f_0\sim\exp[(1/2-c_f)ky]$, localizing toward the UV boundary for $c_f>1/2$ and the IR boundary for $c_f<1/2$, giving hierarchical Yukawas from order-one $c_f$ ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)); $c=1/2$ is the conformal, unlocalized case ([Gherghetta & Pomarol](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/hep-ph/0003129)).
- **Warped towers.** In Randall–Sundrum, $m_n\simeq(n+\alpha/2-1/4)\pi ke^{-\pi kR}$ with $\alpha=|c_f-1/2|,0,1$ for fermions, gauge bosons and gravitons ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).
- **KK gravitons and Newton's law.** Each KK graviton adds a Yukawa term $e^{-m_{\vec n}r}$; the continuum sum reproduces the $1/r^{n+1}$ higher-dimensional potential, while near $r\sim R$ only the first level matters, giving $V\simeq-\frac{G_Nm_1m_2}{r}[1+\alpha e^{-r/R}]$ with $\alpha=8n/3$ from the first-level multiplicity ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)); for a 2-torus $\alpha=16/3$, $\lambda=R$ ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).
- **KK sums in loops (decoupling vs non-decoupling).** Virtual exchange of the full tower of KK gauge bosons shifts electroweak observables by a finite amount only for $d=1$ extra dimension; for $d\ge2$ the sum diverges and must be cut off (at the string scale), though including running couplings renders it finite and over 90% comes from the seven lowest levels ([Masip](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0007048)). Virtual KK-graviton exchange induces dimension-eight operators ([Giudice, Rattazzi & Wells](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9811291)) whose size depends on the UV cutoff and is model-dependent ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)). Gauge couplings acquire power-law running above $M_c$ because $N(\mu,M_c)$ states contribute ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)).
- **Radiative splittings.** Each KK level contains almost degenerate states; one-loop corrections from loops wrapping the extra dimension are well defined and cutoff-independent and are essential for UED phenomenology ([Cheng, Matchev & Schmaltz](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0204342)).
- **Consistent truncation.** Keeping only $n=0$ on $S^1$ is consistent because $n$ is a conserved U(1) charge, so products of singlets never source non-singlets; on other manifolds the question is harder ([Pope lecture notes](https://people.tamu.edu/~c-pope/ihplec.pdf)). Keeping a finite nonzero number of massive modes reintroduces inconsistency ([Duff](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/hep-th/9410046)). For spheres the massless truncations are now established: $D=11$ supergravity on $S^7$ truncates consistently to gauged $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity ([de Wit & Nicolai 1987](https://inspirehep.net/api/literature/230568?fields=titles,authors.full_name,publication_info,abstracts)), with a gap in the original proof filled by Nicolai and Pilch ([Nicolai & Pilch](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.6131)); $S^4$ gives maximal 7D gauged supergravity ([Nastase, Vaman & van Nieuwenhuizen](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9905075)); and all round spheres $S^d$ are generalised parallelisable, recasting the $S^3,S^4,S^5,S^7$ truncations as generalised Scherk–Schwarz reductions ([Lee, Strickland-Constable & Waldram](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.3360)), with exceptional field theory giving consistent truncations on spheres and hyperboloids, e.g. AdS$_5\times S^5$ ([Hohm & Samtleben](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.8145)). For Calabi–Yau compactifications the standard massless effective action is not necessarily a consistent truncation ([Tsimpis](https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2002.09359)), but truncation to pure supergravity with eight supercharges is consistent for any Calabi–Yau threefold ([arXiv:2412.00186](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00186)).

### Examples
- **Klein's charged modes.** In compactified 5D Kaluza–Klein gravity the $n$th Fourier mode of a 5D scalar field has mass $|n|/(r\sqrt\phi)$ and charge proportional to $n$; a Planck-length radius puts the first mode near the Planck mass, about 22 orders of magnitude above the electron ([Overduin & Wesson](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/9805018)).
- **ADD graviton tower.** Each KK graviton couples as $1/M_P$, but summing the almost continuous spectrum gives rates suppressed only by powers of $M_D$; $M_D\sim$ TeV implies $R\sim0.5$ mm for $\delta=2$ ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).
- **Universal extra dimensions.** With all SM fields on $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$ and KK parity, KK particles are pair-produced and the lightest is stable, a dark-matter candidate; the spectrum depends on $\Lambda R$ through loop splittings ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).
- **Thermal field theory.** Compactifying Euclidean time gives the discrete Matsubara frequencies ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaluza%E2%80%93Klein_theory)).

### History
Kaluza's 1921 paper "Zum Unitätsproblem der Physik" proposed a 5D spacetime unifying gravity and electromagnetism ([Kaluza, translation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08616)), imposing a cylinder condition that fields not depend on the fifth coordinate. Klein (1926) made the fifth coordinate a small circle, so fields can be Fourier-expanded and the cylinder condition follows for the light modes ([Overduin & Wesson](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/9805018)); his note "The Atomicity of Electricity as a Quantum Theory Law" appeared in *Nature* 118, 516 ([Crossref](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/118516a0)). Identifying higher modes with charged particles failed because their charge-to-mass ratios matched nothing known ([Overduin & Wesson](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/gr-qc/9805018)). ADD (1998) proposed two or more large flat dimensions in which only gravity propagates, with Standard Model fields localized on a 4D manifold ([ADD](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315); [PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)); Randall–Sundrum (1999) obtained the weak scale from a warped AdS$_5$ slice with weak-scale spin-2 excitations ([Randall & Sundrum](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9905221)).

### Connections
- [Kaluza–Klein Theory](node:Kaluza–Klein%20Theory): the theory whose massive Fourier modes these are.
- [Fourier Analysis](node:Fourier%20Analysis): the tower is the Fourier series on a circle or torus.
- [Laplace–Beltrami Operator](node:Laplace–Beltrami%20Operator) and [Spherical Harmonics](node:Spherical%20Harmonics): eigenvalues give KK masses on curved internal spaces.
- [Compactification](node:Compactification) and [Effective Field Theory of Compactification](node:Effective%20Field%20Theory%20of%20Compactification): the geometry fixes the spectrum.
- [Orbifolds](node:Orbifolds): $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$ removes half the modes and yields chiral zero modes.
- [Large Extra Dimensions](node:Large%20Extra%20Dimensions), [Randall–Sundrum Model](node:Randall–Sundrum%20Model), [Universal Extra Dimensions](node:Universal%20Extra%20Dimensions): model families built on KK towers.
- [Kaluza–Klein Dark Matter](node:Kaluza–Klein%20Dark%20Matter): the lightest KK particle as a relic.
- [Tests of the Inverse-Square Law](node:Tests%20of%20the%20Inverse-Square%20Law): KK gravitons add a Yukawa term.
- [Collider Physics](node:Collider%20Physics): missing-energy and resonance searches.
- [Higgs Mechanism](node:Higgs%20Mechanism): KK vectors eat $A_5^{(n)}$.
- [Supergravity](node:Supergravity) and [Anti-de Sitter Space](node:Anti-de%20Sitter%20Space): sphere truncations and warped geometry.
- [Kähler and Calabi–Yau Manifolds](node:Kähler%20and%20Calabi–Yau%20Manifolds): string compactifications where truncation is subtle.
- [Moduli Spaces](node:Moduli%20Spaces) and [String Theory](node:String%20Theory): KK towers in the distance conjecture.
- [Hierarchy Problem](node:Hierarchy%20Problem): motivation for ADD and RS.

### Common pitfalls
- **Spacing depends on geometry.** $m_n=|n|/R$ holds for a flat circle; tori give $|\vec n|/R$ with growing multiplicity, warped geometries give masses set by $ke^{-\pi kR}$ with spin-dependent offsets ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)), and Scherk–Schwarz twists shift $n\to n+\beta$ ([Pérez-Lorenzana lectures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-ph/0503177)).
- **"No bulk mass on the orbifold."** Only a constant mass is forbidden; odd kink masses $ck\,\epsilon(y)$ are standard ([Gherghetta & Pomarol](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/hep-ph/0003129)).
- **Truncating to massless modes is not automatic.** It is guaranteed on circles and tori but requires proof elsewhere ([Pope lecture notes](https://people.tamu.edu/~c-pope/ihplec.pdf)); a low-energy effective action need not be a consistent truncation ([Tsimpis](https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2002.09359)).
- **Forgetting the moduli.** KK reductions contain moduli such as the dilaton encoding the volume; as unobserved massless fields they make naive models unviable unless stabilized ([nLab](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Kaluza-Klein+mechanism)).

### Open problems
- **Swampland distance conjecture.** At infinite distance in moduli space a tower of light states appears with $m\sim M_0e^{-\lambda\Delta\phi}$; when a circle's radius goes to infinity the tower consists of the KK particles, and the emergent string conjecture says the lightest tower is always a KK or string tower. These are conjectured criteria ([Wikipedia: Swampland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swampland_%28physics%29)), originating in Ooguri and Vafa's conjecture that points at infinity in moduli space are where infinite towers of massless states appear ([Ooguri & Vafa](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0605264)).
- **Consistent truncations beyond universal structures on Calabi–Yau.** Truncations including additional matter multiplets on all universal structures are proposed as ansätze, not yet established ([arXiv:2412.00186](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00186)).
- **Experimental search for KK states.** No KK excitation has been seen; LHC reinterpretations give $1/R>1.4$–$1.5$ TeV for UED with $\Lambda R$ in 5–35, and minimal UED is excluded when combined with relic-density data ([PDG review](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2024/reviews/rpp2024-rev-extra-dimensions.pdf)).
